sources.title: Living or Leaving: Life in the Mekong Delta Region of Viet Nam
sources.temporal_coverage: Report published 2025; the Life in the Mekong Survey covered 5,000 households across 13 delta provinces in April–June 2024; poverty simulations extend to 2050.
sources.methodology: 2024 household survey, official statistics and climate-shock simulations.

sources.title: Report on Children’s Perspectives on Climate Change, Environmental Protection and Socio-Economic Development
sources.organization: UNICEF Viet Nam and Viet Nam Ministry of Planning and Investment
sources.temporal_coverage: Published July 2025; student survey and consultations concern climate perceptions and policies in three Mekong Delta provinces.
sources.methodology: Questionnaire survey of 756 students in six schools, plus focus groups and institutional consultations in three provinces.
sources.limitations: Self-reported school sample; findings do not estimate province-wide prevalence.

sources.title: Insights from Viet Nam: Delivering child-responsive rapid response and resilience-building interventions informed by the principles of Accountability to Affected Populations
sources.organization: UNICEF Innocenti – Global Office of Research and Foresight
sources.temporal_coverage: Case study covers UNICEF response to Typhoon Yagi from September 2024 through June 2025; published December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF case study reports response activities and draws on the government-led multi-sector damage assessment.
sources.limitations: Agency case study; not a counterfactual evaluation of impacts or outcomes.

sources.title: Viet Nam: Typhoon Yagi and Floods Joint Response Plan, September 2024–June 2025
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs on behalf of the UN Country Team and partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Joint response plan issued 27 September 2024 for typhoon and flood response and early recovery through June 2025.
sources.methodology: OCHA-consolidated interagency plan uses government disaster data and sector assessments to set needs, targets and response priorities.
sources.limitations: Planning estimates and commitments, not an outcome evaluation; event-specific and dated.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.65 (printed p.65), climate-exposure regression results from the 2024 survey.
claims.paraphrase: Severe salinity exposure was associated with 17% lower per-capita income; flood and heat exposure with 7% and 6% lower income.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.65–66 (printed pp.65–66), simulated drought-poverty risks.
claims.paraphrase: Through 2050, modeled drought could slow poverty reduction, especially for poorer farming households with fewer assets and less coping capacity.
claims.scenario: World Bank household-income simulation through 2050 under strong-growth and alternative shock-exposure assumptions.
claims.limitations: Simulation, not a forecast; price effects excluded.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Drought can reduce farm income and labor demand, raising poverty risk; printed p.65.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.67–68 (printed pp.67–68), migration and coping section.
claims.paraphrase: Nearly 1.7 million people left the Delta in a decade; migration partly offsets climate-sensitive farm losses, but benefits are uneven.
claims.limitations: Most migrants cite work; climate often acts indirectly, and only 58% of migrant-sending households receive remittances.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Farm households may migrate to offset drought, flood or salinity income losses; printed p.67.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.25 (printed p.25), Mekong Delta environmental vulnerabilities.
claims.paraphrase: High-dyke systems gave wealthier farmers short-term benefits but reduced soil fertility, raised fertilizer dependence and contributed to land consolidation.
claims.limitations: The report summarizes prior studies; it does not estimate distributional effects for all farmers.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.25–27 (printed pp.25–27), children’s perceptions of local climate issues.
claims.paraphrase: Surveyed children identified environmental damage, heat, storms, floods, drought and salt intrusion; 89.9% in Ca Mau cited environmental damage.
claims.limitations: School-based perceptions, not measured hazard exposure.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.30–31 (printed pp.30–31), student survey on climate effects.
claims.paraphrase: Among surveyed students, 48.2% reported climate-related crop loss, 33.5% poverty risk, and 29.5% interrupted schooling or dropout.
claims.limitations: Self-reported survey results; not independently measured losses.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Surveyed children linked climate impacts with crop loss, poverty risk and schooling disruption; printed pp.30–31.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.30 (printed p.30), school-board consultation and Soc Trang account.
claims.paraphrase: Soc Trang consultations linked drought and salinity to crop and income losses, work migration and schooling disruption for children left behind.
claims.limitations: Consultation testimony, not a representative estimate of migration or dropout.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Drought/salinity reduce crops and income, prompting migration that may disrupt children’s schooling; printed p.30.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.49 (printed p.49), conclusions on child-inclusive policy and participation.
claims.paraphrase: Three-province findings identify missing child-specific indicators and targets in climate frameworks; schools and local authorities use participation mechanisms.
claims.limitations: Policy review and student research cover three Mekong Delta provinces.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.3–4 (printed pp.3–4), Yagi impacts on children and families.
claims.paraphrase: Typhoon Yagi damaged about 245,000 homes and displaced families into temporary shelters; 2.65 million children lived in the 11 hardest-hit provinces.
institutions: Viet Nam Disaster and Dyke Management Authority
claims.limitations: The report summarizes national damage estimates; it does not disaggregate displacement by province.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Yagi damage displaced families into temporary shelters; printed p.4.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.4 (printed p.4), livelihood loss and food-security passage.
claims.paraphrase: The storm disrupted farm, fishery and forestry livelihoods, costing 2.3 million workdays and placing over 95,000 people at food-insecurity risk.
claims.limitations: Food insecurity is reported as risk, not confirmed household prevalence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Storm-related livelihood disruption placed households at risk of food insecurity; printed p.4.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.4 (printed p.4), WASH damage and child-protection risk.
claims.paraphrase: Destroyed WASH facilities increased girls’ exposure to gender-based violence; some walked up to 10 kilometres to collect water.
claims.limitations: The case study reports increased exposure, not confirmed GBV incidents.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: WASH destruction increased girls’ GBV exposure and water-fetching burden; printed p.4.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.4–8 (printed pp.4–8), response delivery and feedback mechanisms.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF and government partners combined WASH, learning, protection and cash support, using child and family feedback to adjust recovery assistance.
institutions: Viet Nam Disaster Risk Reduction Partnership
claims.limitations: Agency case study describes response outputs, not independently measured outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.8 (printed p.8), northern provinces and vulnerable populations.
claims.paraphrase: Northern mountain provinces had nearly 18% average poverty versus 4.2% nationally; ethnic minorities were over 55% of the region’s population.
claims.limitations: Figures describe the wider mountainous region and pre-disaster poverty rates.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.8 (printed p.8), typhoon impacts and human-trafficking risk.
claims.paraphrase: The plan says Yagi reversed development gains and deepened hardship in poor affected provinces, increasing human-trafficking risk.
claims.limitations: The plan identifies increased risk; it does not report trafficking incidents caused by Yagi.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Disaster-related reversal of development gains and hardship increased trafficking risk; printed p.8.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.5 (printed p.6), preparedness, evacuation and immediate response.
claims.paraphrase: Before landfall, authorities brought over 51,000 fishing boats and 220,000 crew to shore and evacuated nearly 53,000 people from vulnerable housing.
claims.limitations: Reported preparedness and evacuation outputs; the plan does not estimate avoided losses.

search_audit.query: Viet Nam climate vulnerability named provinces children Mekong Delta drought flood salinity report
search_audit.outcome: Opened World Bank, UNICEF and UN reports; found household survey associations in the Mekong Delta, child perceptions in three named provinces, and Yagi vulnerability in northern provinces.

search_audit.query: Viet Nam climate change drought flood salinity migration poverty livelihood pathways official report
search_audit.outcome: World Bank and UNICEF reports describe climate-linked livelihood loss, migration and schooling disruption; Yagi reporting identifies displacement, food-insecurity risk and protection exposure.

search_audit.query: Viet Nam conflict violence insecurity barriers climate adaptation disaster response trafficking gender-based violence primary report
search_audit.outcome: Yagi reports identify increased trafficking and gender-based violence risks after disaster impacts, but searches found no primary evidence of armed conflict or insecurity obstructing climate adaptation.

search_audit.query: Viet Nam climate adaptation resilience early warning local capacity flood response provincial government report
search_audit.outcome: Reports document pre-landfall evacuation, government-led recovery, UNICEF WASH/cash/protection delivery and community-feedback mechanisms; child policy indicators remain a stated gap.

gaps: No reviewed source established a climate-to-armed-conflict pathway or that armed violence obstructed adaptation; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.
The World Bank climate-income findings are Mekong Delta-wide associations and simulations, not estimates for each province or proof of causality.
UNICEF's climate perceptions are based on a school sample in three delta provinces and should not be read as population prevalence.
Typhoon Yagi reports describe disaster-related trafficking and gender-based violence risks, not confirmed incidents caused by the event.
The updated 2025 National Adaptation Plan PDF at UNFCCC was too large for the browser reader; no claims were taken from indexed snippets.
